name: WIW:NG World Title
notes: Reign list and footnotes from the fed's own World Title history, captured 27 August 2002; later holder from its champions list of 29 November 2002.
epitaph: The fed's own history opens the World Title on 17 May 1999, when Tap Out won a battle royal to become its first champion, and lists 36 reigns across its on-and-off eras to The End's of 18 August 2002. Michael J was its first three-time champion, forfeiting his third reign the next card; Shane Slade won it three times in 2002 and lost the last on 18 August. The November 2002 champions list names Chris Storm.

name: WIW:NG Intercontinental Title
notes: Reign list and footnotes from the fed's own Intercontinental Title history, captured 31 August 2002; later holder from its champions list of 29 November 2002.
epitaph: The fed's own history opens the Intercontinental Title on 17 May 1999 with The Punisher and lists 46 reigns to Chris Storm's of 26 July 2002, among them three by Jack Death and three by Shane Slade. The End won it in a Wrestlefest II cage match on 9 June 2002 and lost it to Storm on 26 July. The November 2002 champions list names Golden Hammer.

name: WIW:NG United States Title
notes: Holders from the fed's own Wrestlefest II and Showdown results pages and its champions list of 29 November 2002; the title's own history page is not held.
epitaph: Its history page is not held; the fed's own cards and champions list give five holders. Erik Erratic carried it into Wrestlefest II, where Shane Slade won it in a Last Man Standing match on 9 June 2002; Larry Stone took it from Ripcord in a title versus title match on 19 July 2002; and the November 2002 champions list names Shorty the Pimp.

name: WIW:NG Television Title
notes: Reign list and footnotes from the fed's own Television Title history, captured 31 August 2002; later holder from its champions list of 29 November 2002.
epitaph: Introduced on 31 January 2000 when Benshaw beat Eric Austin, the Television Title was retired after Chris Storm's reign of July 2000 and revived on 1 December 2000 in a fatal four way. The fed's own history lists 29 reigns to Christian Niels's of 18 August 2002, among them Angelo Deville's of 13 to 27 May 2002 and Bryan Statis's of 30 July to 18 August. The November 2002 champions list names Johnny Fame.

name: WIW:NG Hardcore Title
notes: Reign list and footnotes from the fed's own Hardcore Title history, captured 31 August 2002; its champions list of 29 November 2002 also names Da D'Mon.
epitaph: The fed's own history opens the Hardcore Title on 4 June 1999 when Larry Wood beat Rey Mysterio Jr. in a hardcore match, and lists 51 reigns to Da D'Mon's, won from Larry Stone on 23 July 2002. Raven held it from 29 November 1999 to 13 January 2000, and Trauma and RaZeR were declared co-champions after escaping the Wrestlefest II junkyard together on 9 June 2002.

name: WIW:NG Tag Team Titles
notes: Holders from the fed's own Showdown results pages and its champions list of 29 November 2002; the titles' own history page is not held.
epitaph: Its history page is not held. J Woods and Shorty the Pimp, the Renegades, won it on 19 July 2002 and defended it against Crazy Cooper and Gladiator on 23 July; a Heavy Metal title match was booked for Last Man Standing, and the November 2002 champions list names Project X.

name: WIW:NG XWO World Title
notes: Named on the fed's own Wrestlefest II results page, served under this wing.
epitaph: Contested at Wrestlefest II on 9 June 2002 in a four-man elimination match with special guest referee Zero, which Erik Erratic won from champion Krazy Kris, The End and Masked Magician. Erratic then met e.T.o. for both world titles the same night in a unification match, which e.T.o. won.
